This attribute encodes the available contact channels for a customer. This key is calculated based on the source at which the first engagement and the value is returned. UDF Logic to calculate acquisition channel: UDF receives all the interactions of the customer as Input. Input is divided into multiple lists as specified above. It retrieves the first record from the Profile Management list and retrieves the source name and acquisition source from the record. If the acquisition source is not empty or not null, then the source name is concatenated with acquisition source and the resultant value is returned, else if acquisition source is empty or null then the source name is returned. Note: If the resultant source name is ‘HARTEHANKS’ or ‘CRMLITE’ and if there is a record with the same interaction date with source name other than ‘HARTEHANKS’ or ‘CRMLITE’, then that record is considered as a priority.

Calculated at the end of each month, this field indicates the customer's sales decile within a given brand over the last 12 months. Examining all customer who have made a purchase in the last 12 months, we rank them by the net sales they have generated in the last 12 months, divide them up into 10 groups of equal size based on their ranking, and determine each customer's sales decile based on their grouping, with values ranging from 1 (lowest net sales) to 10 (highest net sales). Non-purchasers are assigned the value 999.

This field indicates the highest sales decile (see decile_key) that the customer has ever acheived since making their first purchase with a given brand. Note: the customer's sales decile is recalcualted at the end of each month, so this field finds the maximum of across all monthly figures for the given customer, ignoring instances where decile_key = 999 (which indicates no decile was assigned).
